name: Pig
description: Pig is a chaotic, high-energy reaction game that turns a standard deck of cards into a test of observation and speed. Played without turns, players rapidly pass cards in a circle to collect a four-of-a-kind. The game's defining feature is the 'Stupid Pose': as soon as one player completes their set and discreetly touches their nose, everyone else must follow suit. The last person to react is the 'Pig' and loses the round. It is a close relative of the game 'Spoons'.

content.text: Pig is a chaotic, high-energy reaction game that turns a standard deck of cards into a test of observation and speed. Played without turns, players rapidly pass cards in a circle to collect a four-of-a-kind. The game's defining feature is the 'Stupid Pose': as soon as one player completes their set and discreetly touches their nose, everyone else must follow suit. The last person to react is the 'Pig' and loses the round. It is a close relative of the game 'Spoons'.
Derived from traditional Victorian-era children's games. It evolved into a popular parlor game alongside 'Spoons' in the mid-20th century.
Large groups are better (5-8 is ideal).
Use exactly 4 cards of the same rank for each player (e.g., if 4 players, use 4 Aces, 4 Kings, 4 Queens, 4 Jacks).
Use exactly 4 cards of the same rank for each player (e.g., if 4 players, use 4 Aces, 4 Kings, 4 Queens, 4 Jacks).
Shuffle the 4-per-player set and deal 4 cards to each person.

items.text: Pig with no stock pile: Use four cards of one rank per player (e.g. 7 players use 28 cards). Shuffle and deal four each. All pass simultaneously to the left until someone has four of a kind.

Pig with a stock pile: Full 52-card pack; four dealt to each player; remainder is stock to dealer's right. Dealer draws from stock; player to dealer's right discards to a pile. When stock is exhausted the discard pile becomes the new stock. Same nose-touch end.

Spoons: Same passing and four-of-a-kind aim, but one fewer spoon than players in the centre. First to get four of a kind takes a spoon; then everyone may grab a spoon. Player left without a spoon loses.
